newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam pegs 1996 GDP growth at 9.34 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam pegs 1996 GDP growth at 9.34 pct.

text.p: Vietnam's gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 9.34 percent this year from 1995 and industrial production increased by 14.1 percent, the government's General Statistics Office said on Tuesday.
It said state sector output increased by 11.7 percent and non-state sector output was up 12.4 percent.

Output from industry with foreign investment was 21.4 percent higher than in 1995, with the oil and gas sector within that category showing growth of 15.2 percent and output of crude oil rising 15.6 percent to 8.805 million tonnes.

The statistics office said in a statement that state sector output growth had slowed because at local levels it was facing strong competition from smuggled goods, goods imported on deferred letters of credit and products of both central level state enterprises and foreign-invested enterprises.
It said the budget deficit was still serious even though revenues had increased and said interest rate and local currency adjustments were too slow during a midyear period of deflation.

The office also said bad management was partially to blame for a record trade deficit of $4.0 billion in 1996, but warned against solving the trade imbalance by seeking to substitute imports rather than develop export-oriented production.
